N = 115,457 dyads from 1,419 players and 2,893 referees

light-skinned players account for 89,019 dyads (1,089 players) with 1,097 red cards (1.23% rate)
dark-skinned players account for 26,438 dyads (330 players) with 358 red cards (1.35% rate)
the model adjusted for eight covariates: games, position, leagueCountry, height, weight, goals, meanIAT, meanExp
21,407 dyads were excluded due to missing skin tone ratings (no player photo available)
9,164 dyads were excluded due to missing covariates (mostly position 6.8%, weight 0.6%, height 0.04%, IAT/Exp 0.12%)
final retention was 79.1% of the original 146,028 dyads
two independent raters coded players on a 5-point scale (1=very light to 5=very dark) from photos
inter-rater correlation was 0.92
the skin tone scale was rescaled to a continuous 0-1 range
the two raters' scores were averaged
the averaged skin tone score was dichotomized at 0.5 (median) into dark (>=0.5) and light (<0.5)
the red card count was converted to a binary indicator
any_red was set to 1 if the dyad had one or more red cards, else 0
dummy variables were created for position and league with reference categories Attacking Midfielder and England
cluster-robust (Huber-White) standard errors were used, clustered by player
clustering by player accounts for within-player correlation across dyads
within-referee clustering was not accounted for, due to computational limitations
no weighting was applied; the analysis is unweighted
no fixed effects were explicitly included
league was controlled for and country-level bias measures were included instead of fixed effects
a logistic regression was fitted: logit[P(any_red=1)] = β0 + β1(dark_skin) + covariates
the adjusted risk difference was calculated via g-computation: predicting probabilities setting dark_skin to 1 for all, then to 0 for all, and taking the mean difference
the standard error of the risk difference was computed via the delta method using the gradient and the cluster-robust covariance matrix of the coefficients
the 95% CI was constructed using a normal approximation, RD ± 1.96×SE(RD)
the two-sided p-value was obtained from a Wald z-test
the log-likelihood was -7,242.3
pseudo R² was 0.073
the model converged successfully in 9 iterations
games had a strong positive effect (β=0.135, p<0.001), more games meaning more red cards via exposure
meanIAT had a positive effect (β=4.18, p<0.001), higher implicit bias associated with more red cards
meanExp had a negative effect (β=-0.43, p=0.021), higher explicit warmth toward whites associated with fewer red cards
